title: REST vs gRPC vs GraphQL
intro: Selecting the optimal communication protocol between clients, gateways, and internal services defines network bandwidth efficiency, schema contracts, and developer velocity.
objectives: Compare REST (HTTP/1.1 JSON), gRPC (HTTP/2 Protobuf), and GraphQL (declarative queries).
Evaluate payload serialization benchmarks: JSON text parsing vs Protobuf binary encoding.
Mitigate the GraphQL N+1 database problem using DataLoader batching.
body:
### Protocol Comparison Matrix

| Feature | REST | gRPC | GraphQL |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Transport** | HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 | HTTP/2 Multiplexed | HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 |
| **Data Format** | JSON (Text) | Protocol Buffers (Binary) | JSON (Text) |
| **Schema Contract** | OpenAPI (Optional) | Strict `.proto` files (Enforced) | GraphQL Schema AST |
| **Performance** | Moderate (Text parsing) | Ultra-Fast (Binary, compact) | Moderate (Query parsing AST) |
| **Best Used For** | Public 3rd-party APIs | Internal Microservices | Complex UI / Mobile Apps |

### Why gRPC Dominates Internal Microservices
Protocol Buffers serializes data into dense binary streams up to 80% smaller than JSON. Because fields are mapped by numeric integer tags rather than text string keys, CPU serialization and deserialization overhead is reduced by $5\times$ to $10\times$.
keyIdea: Use gRPC for high-throughput, low-latency service-to-service calls; use REST for public developer APIs; use GraphQL for rich, client-driven UI applications.

concepts.title: Over-fetching and Under-fetching
concepts.body: REST endpoints often return superfluous data (over-fetching) or require multiple round-trips to assemble a view (under-fetching). GraphQL solves this by letting clients declare exact required fields.

concepts.title: DataLoader
concepts.body: A batching and caching utility that coalesces individual database queries into a single `SELECT WHERE id IN (...)`, eliminating the N+1 problem.

examples: Netflix transitioning internal service communication from REST to gRPC for microsecond efficiency.

quiz.prompt: Why is gRPC significantly faster than standard REST over JSON?
options: Binary Protobuf encoding and HTTP/2 stream multiplexing slash serialization and network overhead
It runs over UDP instead of TCP
quiz.explanation: Binary Protocol Buffers serialization and HTTP/2 multiplexing eliminate text parsing overhead and connection churn.
